scope: All tracked Markdown files in the audit branch at the recorded source_tree_sha. This is a full path inventory; content review remains pending until evidence is recorded.

criteria.label: Read and studied the full Markdown file
Requirements, intended behavior, and acceptance criteria extracted
Claims and requirements traced to real code/configuration
Relevant tests and GitHub Actions workflows verified
GitHub Pages visibility, data source, and controls checked
Internal links and external references checked
Stale, duplicate, or conflicting guidance reconciled

items.notes: Requires focused changes, relevant tests, generated-file discipline, regression tests, and forbids weakening tests or claiming a catalog entry is a live runtime.
Research scope is not a hard model-count limit; evaluate quality, correctness, completeness, speed, efficiency, reliability, safety, and independence with reproducible fixtures and evidence.

Daily scan contract requires deterministic scan, JSON and Markdown artifacts, upload, contract verification, and run summary; it explicitly does not authorize merges, paid compute, weight changes, or unsupported claims.
Requires evidence-backed issue discovery, PR audit, approved repair branches, targeted retries, provenance-bound benchmark states, and immutable historical failures.
Recovery controls must not close, merge, delete, or rewrite PRs from scanner recommendations alone; retry only relevant failures and retain evidence.
Targets AGI-like breadth without AGI claims; requires evidence-driven self-improvement, shared builder roles, uncertainty, verification, and governed autonomy levels.
Uses reference-to-capability-to-benchmark-to-original-system workflow; requires license/provenance checks, independent implementations, holdouts, and original research.
Defines source families, evidence ladder, source scoring, original learning artifacts, reproducibility, and license/privacy boundaries.
Defines platform/command-plane/division/capability contracts, shared workers by default, provenance-preserving migration, and a PR quality bar.
Benchmarks are a learning loop with baseline, gap, hypothesis, sandbox, holdout, transfer, regression, promotion/rejection, and evidence; anti-gaming requires independent tasks.
Defines benchmark lifecycle and no-false-mastery rules; a single pass, routing path, or weakened test is insufficient.
Separates profile completeness from runtime production; required fields and production pack are catalog checks, while runtime needs adapters, sandbox, auth, deployment telemetry.
Requires lossless migration from bot profiles to capability bundles, provenance, explicit relationships, and distinct documented/implemented/tested/mastered states.
Defines source ranking, differential ingestion, original lessons, sandbox exercises, independent holdouts, mastery and regression; licenses/privacy constrain use.
Defines source packages and teacher selection, cheap-first compute, continuous cadence, original tasks, transfer and anti-benchmark-gaming controls.
Defines bounded six-hour workflow windows with checkpointing; gap closure requires measurable tests and regression, not reading a source.
Specifies 65 MasterBot dashboards and benchmark-gap workflows, but the 65-division claim conflicts with 45/46-source records and must remain unresolved pending owner reconciliation.
Defines scoped memory classes, provenance, retention, relevance-based retrieval, contradiction handling, and validation before durable strategy promotion.
Defines a universal action-control acceptance test requiring execution class, prechecks, run ID, captured result, evidence, bounded retry, approval/rollback, and no success claim for skipped work.
Defines an AGI-like product experience without sentience/AGI claims; visible goal, plan, context, tools, risk, execution, evidence, recovery and learning.
Defines LOCAL/REMOTE/READ-ONLY action classes and prohibits browser shell execution, false success, unapproved production changes and hidden failures.
Specifies governed goal-to-outcome action engine, mission graph, verification, recovery, parallelism and money approval; it says 46 divisions, conflicting with 45 and 65 sources.
Defines precheck/execution/evidence/pass/failure routes for every action, staged full certification, safe automation boundaries and health truth model.
Defines 12 master action lanes and action-card contract; roadmap states are goals, not proof of current operation.
Defines action object schema, state machine, DAG execution, checkpoints, bounded retries, independent verification and user-visible execution truth.
Defines unified asset discovery across bots, plans, docs, tools and repos; says 45 divisions and requires discovery-before-mutation and evidence-based completion.
Defines hypothesis-driven repair with explicit uncertainty, evidence-backed system model, active diagnosis, reversible patches, and calibrated self-evaluation without AGI claims.
Defines bot onboarding lifecycle and registry-based discovery, but refers to 46 divisions; this conflicts with other 45/65 division sources.
Defines A0–A5 autonomy levels with universal least-privilege, evidence, bounded retries, rollback and emergency downgrade gates.
Defines failure taxonomy and failure-to-learning loop; explicitly prohibits lowering thresholds or endlessly changing systems without evidence.
Defines benchmark targets as not mastery; requires reproducible baselines, independent evidence, transfer, regression and safe public reporting.
Defines assisted/learning/independent/mastered/blocked states and parallelization constraints for human collaboration benchmarks.

Defines model-owner bootcamp, trust/safety tests, authorized defensive security, 500-model-team concept, PR gates, and interruptible human governance; model slots are a target, not proof of 500 active models.
Defines beginner capability selection, baseline, guided practice, isolated sandbox, holdout/transfer/regression tests, explicit consent and data-use boundaries.
Defines customer-goal-to-curriculum process, compute-saving learning, licensed sources, customer controls and regression maintenance.
Defines shared project graph from intent through sandbox prototype, tests, PR/CI, publish gates and outcome measurement; generated artifacts are not production-ready by default.
Defines benchmark record schema, skill dimensions, baseline/holdout/transfer/regression lifecycle and user-facing diagnostic score breakdowns.
Defines reusable capability graph, targeted learning, evidence provenance and customer namespace isolation; model-independent capability evidence.
Defines static Pages as read-only, issue-based authenticated workflow routing, strict allowlists, two-factor operator/write permission, and PR-only code writes.
Defines device discovery and capability routing through OS/platform permissions; discoverability is not authorization, and support must be verified.
Defines normalized device capability graph and task-to-device planning; distinguishes declared, observed, verified, unavailable and unsupported states.
Contains a 100-idea roadmap with done/planned/future states; defines production-bot acceptance requirements and security/revenue guardrails that need implementation evidence.
Requires every public dashboard value to have source and timestamp; Pages exposes status/evidence and downloads but never secrets or privileged actions.
Contains 150 prioritized improvement suggestions; they are proposals, not completion evidence, and each needs current-state verification.
Provides beginner entry points and explicitly distinguishes a listed bot profile from a fully live specialist.

rules: A Markdown file is not proof that its described capability exists.
Mark a checklist item complete only with a source path, test/workflow result, or Pages evidence link.
Do not delete or rewrite historical Markdown solely to make the audit pass.
Record conflicting statements with both source paths and an owner decision.
Rebuild the inventory whenever Markdown files are added, renamed, or removed.
